messages:
Maya (PM): Heads-up — competitor dropped a tenant-routing toggle that customers keep mentioning. We need a quick call: do we prioritize full parity or ship a focused differentiator first?
Sam (Eng): Curious how many customers actually need exact parity vs a safer UX-approved fallback. Full parity is ~3–4 sprint effort incl infra.
Jordan (Sales): From the field: 5 customers asked specifically this week, 2 are pilots pushing for it. Risk of churn if we can't match their expected routing controls.
Priya (Data): Quick numbers: the pilot cohort shows 18% higher conversion when they can pin routing by tenant. Marginal revenue at stake for those pilots ~ $60k/yr if we lose them.
Li (Design): UX note — parity-level control implies a more complex settings page and a migration path for tenants. We can mock a simplified surface that looks familiar to customers but hides advanced knobs. :thinking_face:
Sam (Eng): Proposal: "parity-lite" (routing toggle + per-tenant fallback + logging) — implement core control without exposing full advanced policy language. Targets: latency delta <10ms, opt-in flag, fallback to default routing on error. Est. 2 sprints for eng + 1 for infra/config.
Maya (PM): Nice. What's the risk vector? will it block other roadmap items?
Sam (Eng): Main risk is stateful rollout complexity (per-tenant config stores + KV caching). We'll need a migration plan to avoid cache explosions. Also need canary rollback hooks.
Priya (Data): Add a metric requirement: launch only if error-rate for routed requests <0.5% over 48h during canary and retention lift >=6% in pilot segment.
Jordan (Sales): If we can promise an opt-in pilot in 6 weeks, I can lock 2 pilots. That matches their procurement windows.
Li (Design): I'll produce a compact settings mock that surfaces the toggle and an "advanced" link. Keep language consistent with Console (no new jargon). ETA 4 business days.
Maya (PM): Draft launch criteria so we can agree: 
- canary at 5% tenants for 7 days, error-rate <0.5%
- documented fallback and rollback (runbook)
- design + help docs live
- Sales pilot commitment for at least 2 customers
- perf overhead <10ms p50
If all met, go/no-go for GA.
Sam (Eng): Agreed. For rollout I'll use this feature-flag flow: 
```
releases toggle --feature tenant-routing-parity --on --scope=5% 
# monitor: infra/tenant-routing-canary
```
And this minimal canary config: 
```
canary:
  percent: 5
  duration_days: 7
routes:
  - match: tenant.routing
    variant: routing-lite-v1
    fallback: routing-default
```
I'll hook in autoscale policy for the canary group.
Maya (PM): Budget/priority tradeoff? This would bump ~40% of next sprint capacity for Eng. Is that acceptable?
Sam (Eng): We can defer one low-impact infra tech debt ticket. If product signs off, we can start next sprint.
Jordan (Sales): I'll get a commitment from the pilots that they will run the canary and share metrics. That helps Priya validate retention.
Priya (Data): I'll prepare dashboards: per-tenant retention, latency, and error-rate. Need table of pilot tenant IDs.
Li (Design): Punting large policy language until after parity-lite. We should call the feature "tenant routing toggle (beta)".
Maya (PM): Ok action items:
- Sam: finalize infra runbook + estimate (due EOD Thu)
- Li: compact settings mock + microcopy (4d)
- Priya: dashboard skeleton + metric thresholds (3d)
- Jordan: confirm 2 pilots and list of tenant IDs (5d)
Maya (PM): If we hit the launch criteria during canary, we GA. If not, rollback and iterate. Agree? :thumbsup:
Sam (Eng): :thumbsup: I'll add the feature flag and the rollback script now.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy created: tenant-routing-parity-canary window 2024-12-06T08:00Z -> 2024-12-13T08:00Z
Jordan (Sales): I'll update the pilot contracts language to reflect "beta" and rollback risks.
Maya (PM): Thanks all — we'll reconvene after Sam's infra runbook.
Sam (Eng): Filing the PR and opener ticket: infra#4821, feature#9876. Link: https://redwood.internal/infra/4821
Priya (Data): Will post the dashboard link in thread once ready.
Maya (PM): Closing loop — this is a tactical path that preserves our differentiator roadmap while addressing immediate churn risk. We'll treat full policy parity as next-cycle work.
